Vanessa Automation 1.2.043.42-itl-r14

This binary distribution is built from Pr-Mex/vanessa-automation
tag 1.2.043.42, commit a0ce2ee9803dd69be52f682e5cf49e0938fd33f1,
with source-controlled ITL patches.

The upstream compatibility version remains 1.2.043.42. The downstream
revision itl-r14 identifies the patch and is not an upstream release.

Vanessa Automation is distributed under the BSD 3-Clause License. The
complete upstream copyright notice, license conditions, and disclaimer are
included in LICENSE at the root of the binary distribution.

The patch preserves the ITL MCP callbacks, selected-feature tree, row navigation,
TestClient port ownership, and the paired file-code channel with VAExtension.
It also backports progress-token and independent If/Else fixes and replaces
ping-based wait fallbacks with local sleep commands.

The patched VAExtension must be built and qualified with this EPF before
installation.

The HTML hyperlink and button forms retain the client click path and remove
unused server controls whose command handlers are absent in upstream source.

The report variant layout uses its requested report manager for the existing
UniversalReport-specific calls and their four/three-argument fallback. The two
system-form wrappers resolve their platform-owned sysForm namespace through
a closed client helper and retain their opening and callback behavior.

The canonical cumulative patch pins full Git indexes. It retains all r3 source
hunks and can be reproduced independently of repository object counts.

Revision itl-r8 retains r4 and preserves primary tabular-cell assertion details
when optional attachment creation fails. Secondary attachment errors are appended;
comparison, retry and failure semantics remain unchanged. This recipe and its
paired extension require exact native qualification before installation/release.

Current-window expression failures are rethrown after the existing log entry. Existing wait limits, successful execution and optional helper close behavior are retained.

Diagnostic PNG I/O failures are logged separately and finish the original error report through its existing owner. Explicit screenshot failures and successful attachments retain their contracts.

Pre-execution feature rejection uses a qualified MCP error; pending request notifications are cleared through existing setters. Runtime, transport and unknown execution failures retain their existing handling.

Revision itl-r10 retains r8. An ITL agent launch is marked by
ITLAgentLaunch in the VAParams dopparams structure; manual launches keep the
upstream behavior. In an agent launch the plain built-in code steps run through
the paired file-code channel without opening a TestClient form or using the OS
clipboard, the TestClient window is not activated on connection, OS keyboard and
mouse input activates the TestClient immediately before it, and the all-windows
screenshot captures the TestClient process window instead of the whole screen.

Revision itl-r11 retains r10. In an agent launch the clipboard code steps
(на клиенте / на сервере / в привилегированном режиме через буфер обмена)
run through the same paired file-code channel as the plain code steps, so an
exception or a compilation error fails the step with its original text; without
the channel an agent launch rejects them. Manual launches keep the clipboard route.
run_scenario with filePath reloads the current file text in the all,
reloadAndRun and reloadAndRunFromLine modes, rejects a file changed during the
load and reports featureFile and featureSha256 of the executed bytes. An MCP feature load rejects a character that XML 1.0 forbids
with file:line:column. navigate_to_row reports success only for a settled current
row that matches the criteria and otherwise reports the actual row. For an HTML
document field, click_hyperlink uses the HTML document click; an agent launch
retries a failed click by text in the TestClient DOM through the paired
VAExtension form, opening closed details ancestors, and lists the anchors found.

Revision itl-r12 retains r11. A TestClient port is occupied only while a TCP
socket listens on it: on Windows a netstat row whose foreign address is the
unspecified 0.0.0.0:0 or [::]:0, independent of the system language, and on
Linux a LISTEN row of ss -ltn. TIME_WAIT, ESTABLISHED and CLOSE_WAIT sockets
left by a closed client no longer make its assigned port busy, so the client
restarts on that port instead of failing with ITL_TESTCLIENT_NO_FREE_PORT.

Revision itl-r14 retains r12 and serves hidden agent TestClients through the ITL
window helper: an agent launch with the window channel starts the client hidden,
takes keyboard and mouse only inside a user-approved lease confirmed by the
foreground process, and captures only the client process window. Manual launches
and agent launches without the channel keep the r12 behavior.
